phase3_findings.description: stream_request's docstring at line 105 still promises 'Yields text chunks as they arrive', but the rewritten body drains the whole text_stream inside one asyncio.to_thread call at line 124 and yields every chunk only afterwards at line 126; the inline comment at lines 112-118 describes the new behavior correctly, so docstring and comment contradict each other. Reported in earlier iterations with no fix decision recorded.

truncate_messages' docstring calls returning False 'never an error', but the user-id mismatch branch at line 119 leaves the conversation holding the cancelled call's messages, the same consequence the sibling missing-seam arm in query_database.py logs at ERROR; neither the bool nor the caller's single INFO line distinguishes the three outcomes. Unreachable with the shipped single-user _StaticUserResolver.

Line 123 deletes the message tail with del conversation.messages[length:] from outside the model, while Conversation.add_message stamps updated_at alongside every append, so after a cancel rollback updated_at still reflects the cancelled turn; that field is the sort key of list_conversations at line 90.

The comment blocks added at lines 213-236, 251-259 and 425-434, with the same shape at 114-122 and 155-171, spend most of their length on provenance and unreachability analysis rather than on the wrong edit a maintainer might make; the runner and runtime.py comments are the right shape by contrast.

_ConversationQueueEntry is anemic: its refcount invariant is maintained by hand at three sites (lines 175-178, 179 and 149), users is a public mutable int with no acquire/release behavior on the type, and _release_queue_entry line 150 tests users <= 0 rather than == 0, so a future double release would silently delete a still-live entry. Shipped paths are correct.

The store seam is untyped: truncate_messages is declared only on BoundedConversationStore while the ConversationStore base class declares only async methods, so the caller probes with getattr and degrades to an ERROR log at lines 236-247, and both helper signatures type the dependency as agent: Any at lines 195-197 and 213-215.

truncate_messages takes a raw user_id: str while every sibling takes a User and unwraps the identity itself, so an unrelated string is a well-typed argument that silently skips the rollback; the caller's baseline_user_id = "" at lines 422-423 of query_database.py is kept out of the call only by the queued_id is not None guard at line 456, and the identity precondition is not raised the way length < 0 is at line 117.

_conversation_turn encodes two independent decisions in one str | None yield — which conversation id to roll back and whether a turn lock was taken — and the caller at lines 422-457 re-derives the baseline from two separately initialized locals, so illegal combinations are guard-dependent rather than unrepresentable.

The rewritten Note asserts 'so its health check keeps answering', but /healthz exists only in the HTTP transport's path normalizer while the same paragraph recommends stdio mode, where there is no health endpoint; the acceptance criterion asks only for the 'does not stop the server from accepting other requests' half, which the sentence already carries.

The added block cites cleanup-error-handling.md for the shutdown-wait claim and cites the same page again in the next sentence for how cancellation unwinds, reading as though two different pages were meant. Both statements are true.

test_profile_row_cap_reaches_offloaded_runner exercises PostgresRunner only, while MySQL and SQLite each gained the same asyncio.to_thread hop and read effective_row_cap inside the thread, so switching either to loop.run_in_executor would silently fetch the base max_rows with no failing test.
